text:
Marco: heads-up — after yesterday's runtime change to continuous batching the short-prefix p95/p99 climbed for a subset of traffic. hit-rate for prefix cache down ~18% on low-token requests. anyone else seeing this?
Anita: saw the alert. looks correlated with that batching-optimizer rollout at ~23:00 UTC.
Jess: confirmed on canary traces — queueing skew increased: more heterogenous batch composition, cold-kv entries getting pushed through.
Rob: can you paste the profiling snapshot? kernel selection metrics + batch composition?
Marco: attached quick summary: 
```
agg(threads, latency): p50 32ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms (short prompts)
cache_hit_rate(prefix): 0.62 -> 0.51
batch_size_mean: 7.3 -> 9.8
kernel_choice: cudnn->fused-attn increased for long seqs
```
Anita: interesting that mean batch size grew — continuous batching grouped more mixed-length requests, so KV warmup probability per request down.
Jess: my hypothesis: affinity between similar prefix keys got diluted when the queueing window widened. We optimized for throughput but increased cross-key mixing.
Rob: can we test reducing the max_window_ms and biasing by prefix-hash affinity? i.e. if requests share prefix-id push them to same mini-batch.
Marco: agree. small experiment suggestion: add affinity bucketing + keep-alive for KV to favor same-worker placement for a short period.
Anita: note: kernel selection also matters — larger batches sometimes pick different kernel paths that hurt short-tail latency. need to ensure kernel decision uses latency-SLO weight, not only throughput.
Jess: ran a quick ablation on canary: set window_ms 12 -> 6 and enabled prefix-bucket (8 buckets) -> cache_hit_rate up to 0.60 and p95 back to ~170ms. throughput steady.
Rob: great. any regressions in GPU utilization or token/sec?
Jess: minor fluctuation, token/sec -2%. acceptable.
infra-bot: deploy event: rollout/continuous-batching v2 started at 2026-03-17T23:08:12Z by deploy-bot (id: cb-v2).
deploy-bot: note: v2 enabled dynamic windowing + kernel auto-switch heuristics.
Marco: I want a repro harness to stress mixed-length arrival patterns. can someone add a synthetic workload: 70% short-prompts (<=8 tokens prefix) and 30% long to replay across worker pool?
Anita: I'll stitch a JMeter script and add a param sweep for window_ms and bucket_count.
Jess: also capture kv occupancy and per-worker key-eviction counters. use `kv_stats.export()` every 10s.
Marco: don't forget to log kernel_choice per batch and batch composition vector, e.g. `[short_count,long_count,avg_len]`.
Rob: if affinity bucketing helps, we should also consider fallback for low-volume tenants where bucketing reduces batching efficiency — maybe only enable bucket affinity when partial hit_rate < threshold.
Anita: good point. adaptive policy: if cache_hit_rate < 0.55 and rps>50 then enable affinity.
Jess: quick note: I saw a path where KV warmup race occurs when a warmed key gets evicted before subsequent request due to worker churn. proposing a short soft-ttl renewal on hit to extend live window by +200ms.
Marco: that could help. but be careful about memory growth. cap renewals per-key per-second.
Rob: timeline? can we A/B this on 10% of traffic tomorrow?
Anita: yes — I'll schedule canary with three arms: (1) baseline v2, (2) v2+affinity bucketing, (3) v2+reduced-window.
Jess: I'll prepare dashboards: prefix-hit-rate, p95 short, kernel-switch-rate, eviction-rate. link: https://perf.internal.redwood/d/affinity/continuous-batching (placeholder).
Marco: thanks. last thing — add an eval prompt set to measure semantic impact (we don't want quality regressions if kernel quantization path changes).
Rob: +1. keep token-gen samples for offline diffs.
infra-bot: canary scheduled: affinity-buckets on eng-runtime-canary at 2026-03-18T08:00:00Z.
Marco: awesome. if we see improvement we'll roll to 50% then full.
Jess: posting quick results snippet after first 2 hours of canary later today. :thumbsup:
Rob: thanks all.
Anita: creating GH PR for the affinity bucket scheduler and the window param toggle — will link here when ready.
Marco: ping me when PR lands.
Jess: PR #4127 linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4127
Rob: cool. I'll review tomorrow morning.
Marco: closing loop — good detective work y'all.
